newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: South African long bonds ended a buoyant week strong -- although off their intraday highs -- after moving to their best levels in a year following aggressive early morning buying.
Friday's gains crowned a week characterised by healthy demand which saw bonds rally with rates falling just under 40 basis points on the week.
At 1426 GMT government's benchmark R150 stock was at 14.735 percent from 14.90 percent overnight and an intraday best level of 14.63 percent.

The market was boosted by a flurry of positive financial briefings, including Finance Minister Trevor Manuel's adjustment budget where he announced that government was on track to achieve a deficit of 5.1 percent of gross domestic product.
Reserve Bank Governor Chris Stals' comments that interest rates might be cut later rather than sooner dissapointed the market but were soon shrugged off as bullish sentiment prevailed.
"Buckle your seatbelt, we're going down," is how one bond trader described the Friday morning buying spree.
Others said local and foreign demand was on the back of strength in the U.S. market which came down sharply from Thursday's levels.
The market retraced during the mid-morning session but traders said the outlook for next week was rosy.
"Players are still gearing themselves for the downside," one senior trader said although he added there could be some sideways movement at the start of the week as players took a breather.
Foreigners sold a net 20.84 million rands worth of South African bonds on Thursday after buying 477.84 million on Wednesday, the Bond Exchange said.
Nominal cumulative turnover was 43.66 billion rand on Thursday -- a settlement date -- from 5.6 billion rand on Wednesday.
The rand ended a nervous trading day near its previous closing levels as the market struggled to find direction following a volatile week.
At 1626 GMT it was trading at 4.4145/4175 on the dollar from 4.4105/4135 late on Thursday.

The unit was little changed from last Friday's closing levels. The feature of the week was a dramatic fall mid-week on comments by Reserve Bank governor Chris Stals that the rand's recent rally could be a slight "over-adjustment".
But the unit recovered on subsequent bullish comments by Stals.
"It's been a hectic week and the market is struggling for direction," a senior forex trader noted.
Another expected the rand to move in its new-found 4.39 to 4.45 range at the start of next week and said the underlying mood was still positive.
"People are still looking at any levels to sell dollars," she said.
The next major event, traders agreed, was the March 12 1997/1998 budget and trade could be quietish in the lead-up to that event.
Against the crosses, the rand was last trading at 7.1602/1695 against sterling from 7.1543/1651 late on Thursday and it was trading at 0.3814/3818 marks from 0.3819/3824 marks previously.
South Africa's money market shortage rose to 10.167 billion rand on Thursday from 9.171 billion rand on Wednesday, the Reserve Bank said on Friday.
Three-month NCDs rates were quoted steady at between 16.40 to 16.65 percent, while the 90-day BA rate was also unchanged at between 15.80 to 16.05 percent bid.
-- Vera von Lieres, Johannesburg newsroom 27 11 482 1003
